title: Greedy Single-Step and Double-Step Construction
approach_explanation: The problem asks for the minimum number of jumps to reach position x such that each jump length is not divisible by k. The minimum possible number of moves is 1. We can achieve 1 move if the direct jump length x is not divisible by k. This occurs whenever k > x or x % k != 0. If x is divisible by k, a single jump is forbidden, but we can always reach x in exactly 2 moves by jumping to x - 1 first (since x - 1 is not divisible by k) and then taking a second jump of length 1 (since 1 is not divisible by k, given k >= 2).

code_breakdown.explanation: Read the number of test cases t and loop through each test case, reading the target position x and the forbidden divisor k.
If k is strictly greater than x, then x itself cannot be divisible by k. Therefore, we can reach x in 1 move by jumping directly to x.
If k <= x but x is not divisible by k, a single jump of length x is valid and takes us directly to the target in 1 move.

If x is divisible by k, 1 move is impossible. We construct a 2-move solution by jumping to x - 1 (which leaves a remainder of k - 1 when divided by k, hence valid) and then jumping 1 unit to land exactly on x.

complexity_analysis.time_justification: For each of the t test cases, a constant number of arithmetic operations and comparisons are performed, resulting in $O(1)$ time per test case and $O(t)$ total time.
complexity_analysis.space_justification: No additional data structures or dynamic memory allocations are used; only a few scalar variables are maintained.

strengths: Clear, concise conditional logic covering all logical cases.
edge_cases_handled: Target x smaller than k (k > x).
Target x perfectly divisible by k (x % k == 0).
